chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Hasan, the teacher, from Ahmad bin Ali al-Esbahani, from Ibrahim bin Muhammad al-Thaqafi, that he said: We were told by Abu'l-Hasan Ali bin Muhammad, a teacher from the people of Ray, that he said: We were told by Mansur bin Abbas, and Hasan bin Ali bin Nadr, from Sa'id bin Nadr, from Ja'far bin Muhammad, peace be upon them both, that he said:

Property and children are the ornamentation of the life of this world, and eight rak'at from the last part of the night and the Witr is the ornamentation of the Hereafter, and it may be that Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, gathers them to some people.

key_terms.زِينَةُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا: ornamentation of the life of this world

ai.seo_question: What is considered the ornamentation of the Hereafter according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this narration to distinguish between the transient 'ornament' of material life and the enduring spiritual beauty of the Hereafter, specifically highlighting the eight rak'at of night prayer (Salat al-Layl) alongside Witr. This reflects the Shia emphasis on voluntary night worship as a means of purifying the soul and attaining closeness to God, balancing worldly responsibilities with spiritual devotion. The hadith acknowledges that while these realms are distinct, divine grace may allow the righteous to possess both, as seen in the Prophets and Imams.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Hasan, the teacher, from Ahmad bin Ali al-Esbahani, from Ibrahim bin Muhammed al-Thaqafi, that he said: We were told by Abu’l-Hasan, Ali bin Muhammed, a teacher from the people of Ray, that he said: We were told by Mansur bin Abbas, and Hasan bin Ali bin Nadr, of Sa’eed bin Nadr, of Ja’far bin Muhammed, peace be upon them both, that he said:

Property and children are the ornamentation of the life of this world, and eight rak’at from the (prayer of the) last (part of the) night and the Witr [1] is the ornamentation of the Hereafter, and it may be that Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, gathers them to some people.
